HTML describes the structure and meaning of a document. A browser parses it into a tree called the DOM. CSS changes how that tree looks; JavaScript can change how it behaves.
Start with a document skeleton
Use <!doctype html> to select standards mode. The html element wraps the document. Put metadata in head and visible content in body. Set lang="en" so assistive technologies know the language.
Give every page an identity

lessons.summary: Understand the building blocks of every interface.

Most elements have an opening tag, content, and a closing tag:

Hello

Attributes configure elements

Classes are reusable labels

lessons.title: Headings & meaningful text
lessons.summary: Give your content a readable hierarchy.
learn: Headings outline the page
h1 through h6 express hierarchical sections, not font sizes. Nest heading levels logically; use CSS to change their appearance. Screen reader users often jump between headings.
Emphasis has meaning
Use strong for importance and em for stress emphasis. Use p for paragraphs, not repeated br elements. br is appropriate for meaningful line breaks such as an address or poem.
Represent code correctly
code marks a code fragment and pre preserves whitespace. Escape < as < and & as & when showing source as text. Use blockquote for extended quoted content, not indentation.

lessons.title: Links & navigation
lessons.summary: Connect pages, sections, and destinations.
learn: Links navigate; buttons act
An a element with href navigates to a URL. Use a button for an action such as opening a dialog. Text like “Read the accessibility guide” is more useful than “Click here”.
Relative and absolute URLs
https://example.com/ is absolute. /about is relative to the site root; ./about is relative to the current document. #contact navigates to an element with id="contact".
New tabs need care

lessons.title: Images & alternative text
lessons.summary: Use images without leaving anyone behind.
learn: Two essential attributes
img uses src for the resource and alt for a text alternative. Describe the image’s purpose in context, not every visual detail. For decorative images, use alt="" so screen readers skip them.
Prevent layout shifts
Set width and height to establish an aspect ratio before the image loads. CSS can make the actual width responsive. Lazy-load below-the-fold images, not the important hero image.
Caption a figure
figure groups self-contained media. figcaption provides a visible caption. A visible caption and alt text serve related but different purposes.

lessons.title: Semantic page architecture
lessons.summary: Build landmarks, not a soup of divs.
learn: Landmarks make pages navigable
Use header for introductory content, nav for major navigation, main for the dominant content, and footer for related closing information. Typically only one non-hidden main is present.
Section versus article
article is self-contained content that could stand on its own. section groups a thematic part of a document, usually with a heading. A div is appropriate when only a styling wrapper is needed.
Semantics are not appearance
An aside is tangential content; it does not mean “anything on the right”. Native semantics survive CSS changes and help search engines and assistive technologies understand a page.

Supply context

lessons.title: Forms & labels
lessons.summary: Collect input with native, accessible controls.
learn: Forms connect controls to submission
form groups fields for a submission. action defines the destination and method defines the HTTP method. GET places values in the URL; POST sends them in the request body. Neither replaces HTTPS.
Every control needs a name
The name attribute is the key sent to the server. An id alone is not submitted. Associate label for="email" with input id="email"; a placeholder is not a substitute for a visible label.
Use explicit button types
Inside forms, a button defaults to submit. Set type="button" for non-submission actions. This practice lab is a sandbox: forms demonstrate markup but do not send data.

lessons.title: Input types & validation
lessons.summary: Let the browser do the useful work.
learn: Choose appropriate types

email, url, number, date, checkbox, and radio provide native behavior. Use inputmode to hint at a keyboard when type alone is not right. Telephone numbers are text-like identifiers, not arithmetic numbers.
Declare constraints
required prevents empty submission; minlength and maxlength constrain text; min, max, and step constrain numeric/date-like fields. type="email" checks syntax, not whether an address exists.
Validation is not security

Client validation improves feedback and can be bypassed. Servers must validate every received value too. Describe expected formats before users encounter errors, and associate help text using aria-describedby.

SEO starts with usability

lessons.title: Keyboard & accessible names
lessons.summary: Build interfaces more people can use.
learn: Native elements first
Use a real button rather than a clickable div. Native controls provide focus and keyboard activation automatically. ARIA adds semantics but does not implement behavior.
Keep a logical focus order

DOM order should match reading order. Avoid positive tabindex values that create a competing order. tabindex="0" includes a custom element in normal focus order; -1 supports programmatic focus without tab sequence inclusion.
Names and instructions

Visible labels are usually best. Icon-only buttons need an accessible name such as aria-label. Keep focus indicators visible. Use aria-describedby for supporting instructions, not as the primary name.

lessons.title: Selectors & relationships
lessons.summary: Target exactly what you intend.
learn: Basic selectors
A type selector such as p matches elements by name. .card matches a class, #hero an id, and [disabled] an attribute. Reusable classes are useful building blocks.
Combinators describe relationships
.card p matches any descendant paragraph. .card > p matches direct children. h2 + p matches an immediately following sibling, while h2 ~ p matches later sibling paragraphs.
Group and inspect

lessons.title: Cascade, specificity & inheritance
lessons.summary: Understand why a style wins.
learn: The cascade is more than specificity
The browser considers origin and importance, cascade layers, specificity, scoping proximity where relevant, then source order. A later rule wins only when earlier priorities tie.
Specificity weights

Within the same origin/layer/importance, ids outweigh classes, attributes, and pseudo-classes, which outweigh type selectors. :where() contributes zero specificity. Avoid using !important as a default repair tool.
Inheritance is selective

Text properties such as color and font-family often inherit. Margin and border generally do not. inherit, initial, unset, and revert have distinct reset behaviors. Use DevTools computed styles to trace the winner.

lessons.title: The box model
lessons.summary: Master the geometry behind every layout.
learn: Four nested regions
Each element has content, padding, border, and margin. Padding is inside the border; margin separates the box from neighbors. Backgrounds paint through padding by default.
Predictable sizing
With content-box, width covers only content. With border-box, width includes padding and border. A common reset sets box-sizing: border-box on all elements and pseudo-elements.
Margin behavior
Adjacent vertical block margins can collapse in normal flow. Flex and grid items behave differently. If spacing surprises you, inspect box geometry in DevTools rather than inserting empty elements.

lessons.summary: Design beyond fixed pixels.

px is a CSS pixel, not necessarily a device pixel. rem relates to root font size, em to a relevant font size, and percentages depend on the property and containing block.
Viewport units
vw and vh relate to viewport dimensions. Modern svh, lvh, and dvh address mobile browser UI changes. For long content, prefer min-height over a rigid height.
Fluid limits
min(), max(), and clamp() express responsive constraints. clamp(2rem, 6vw, 5rem) has a minimum, a preferred fluid value, and a maximum. A max-width in ch can limit reading line length.

Custom properties

Define tokens such as --accent: #f97316 on :root and consume them with var(--accent). They cascade and normally inherit. var(--accent, coral) supplies a fallback when a variable is missing or invalid as a custom property.
Contrast is functional

Check text contrast against its actual background, including transparent layers. WCAG AA generally requires 4.5:1 for normal text and 3:1 for large text. A bright accent is not automatically readable.

Readable body text
A unitless line-height around 1.5–1.7 works for many body fonts. Limit line length, avoid overly small text, and test at zoom. Large headings often need tighter line heights.
Loading fonts

Block boxes generally stack in the block direction; inline content flows within lines. Writing mode affects these axes. A span is inline by default; a div is block by default.
Choose display based on layout
inline-block creates an atomic inline box that can accept dimensions. flex and grid establish new layout contexts. display: none removes an element from layout and generally the accessibility tree.
Visibility and overflow

lessons.summary: Place elements without fighting the layout.

relative preserves the original space and can establish a containing block. absolute leaves normal flow and positions relative to a containing block, often the nearest positioned ancestor.
Sticky versus fixed

fixed usually anchors to the viewport, though some properties can establish a different containing block. sticky stays in flow, then sticks within its scrolling context when a threshold such as top is reached.
Stacking contexts
z-index is not globally comparable across every element. Transforms, opacity below 1, and other properties can create stacking contexts. A huge z-index cannot escape an ancestor’s stacking context.

Establish containment

Structural selectors

Do not remove outlines without a strong replacement. Pair focus styles with hover styling. Disabled states should remain legible and must be functionally disabled, not merely grey.

Transitions interpolate changes
A transition animates between property values when a state changes. Declare specific properties rather than transition: all. Duration, delay, and easing shape the experience.

Transform and opacity are often cheaper to animate than layout properties such as width or top, but performance still depends on the element and browser. Avoid large motion and support reduced motion.

@keyframes names a sequence of styles. Use from/to or percentage stops. animation applies the name, duration, timing function, and iteration count.
Loops and state

linear produces a steady spin; ease creates acceleration/deceleration. animation-fill-mode controls how styles apply outside the active animation interval. Infinite animation should be purposeful, not distracting.

Replace rather than just accelerate
Remove large-scale transforms and continuous loops where possible. Keep essential state changes clear without relying on animation completion events.

JDBC uses Connection, PreparedStatement, and ResultSet. A driver connects to a specific database. Prepared statements keep SQL structure separate from parameter values.
In practice

Typical code is connection.prepareStatement("SELECT name FROM users WHERE id = ?"), then statement.setLong(1, id), then executeQuery(). Close resources with try-with-resources. For multi-step writes, disable auto-commit, commit on success, and roll back on failure.
Watch out for

Never concatenate untrusted values into SQL. Parameters substitute values, not arbitrary table names or SQL syntax. This lab has no JDBC driver or database, so the exercise checks the parameterized statement structure only.

lessons.title: Testing, Maven & Gradle
lessons.summary: Make builds repeatable and behavior verifiable.
learn: How it works
Maven and Gradle declare dependencies and build steps. A conventional layout separates src/main/java and src/test/java. JUnit tests assert behavior and run as part of a build.
In practice
Pin dependency versions, run tests in CI, and separate fast unit tests from integration tests that need infrastructure. In this dependency-free lab, throw AssertionError for a failed assertion.
Watch out for
Java assert statements are disabled unless enabled with -ea. Do not rely on them for user-input validation. A passing build does not remove the need for security and compatibility checks.

lessons.title: JVM memory, logging & secure services
lessons.summary: Connect language skills to reliable application behavior.
learn: How it works
The JVM manages heap memory and garbage collection; each thread also needs stack space. Reachable objects remain live, so caches and listeners can retain memory unintentionally.
In practice

Profile before tuning, bound caches and request sizes, and log useful event context without passwords or tokens. At API boundaries, authenticate identity, authorize each action, validate input, and return deliberate status codes.
Watch out for

Garbage collection does not prevent memory leaks through unwanted references. Do not deserialize untrusted native Java objects. Frameworks such as Spring add routing and dependency injection but do not replace these fundamentals.

lessons.title: Build an inventory model
lessons.summary: Combine records, collections, validation, and tests.
learn: How it works
A small domain model should make invalid states difficult to create. Records can represent items; maps can index them by stable ID; methods can enforce rules for updates.
In practice
Start with deterministic business logic and tests before adding database persistence or an HTTP framework. Use integer minor units or BigDecimal for prices and explicit quantity validation.
Watch out for
Do not expose mutable internal collections directly. A real multi-user service also needs transactions, authorization, and concurrency control; an in-memory exercise is not a production backend.
